#🍁🍁 Machine-learning testing in TCGA-LIHC full cohort

The three trained models are externally evaluated in the TCGA-LIHC full cohort and further assessed in a balanced sensitivity-analysis cohort.

### Analysis step 1

```{r b6-analysis-step-1}
rm(list = ls())

options(timeout = 100000) 
options(scipen = 20)
options(stringsAsFactors = F)

set.seed(123)

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 0: Load required packages

This chunk clears the active workspace where specified, sets analysis options, and loads the packages required for the following steps.

```{r b6-module-0-load-required-packages}
library(data.table)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)

```

Interpretation: successful completion confirms that the required packages are available and the analysis environment is ready.

### Module 1: Set input files in current directory

This chunk defines the input files and analysis settings, creates the requested output directory where applicable, and checks that required files are available.

```{r b6-module-1-set-input-files-in-current-direct}
## Module 1. Set input files in current directory
training_model_file <- "GSE54503_ML_training_3models_157hypoDMRs.Rdata"

tcga_full_file <- "step0.2_TCGA_LIHC_output.Rdata"

outdir <- "ML_157_hypo_DMRs_full_cohort"

if (!dir.exists(outdir)) {
  dir.create(
    outdir,
    recursive = TRUE
  )
}

if (!file.exists(training_model_file)) {
  stop(paste0("Training model file not found: ", training_model_file))
}

if (!file.exists(tcga_full_file)) {
  stop(paste0("TCGA full cohort file not found: ", tcga_full_file))
}

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 2: Load trained models and training information

This chunk loads the trained models and verifies that all objects required for external testing are present.

```{r b6-module-2-load-trained-models-and-training-}
load(training_model_file)

required_objects <- c(
  "model_glmnet",
  "model_rf",
  "model_svm",
  "dmr.tbl",
  "dmr.cpg.list",
  "feature_name_map",
  "ml_df"
)

missing_objects <- required_objects[!sapply(required_objects, exists)]

if (length(missing_objects) > 0) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Missing objects in training Rdata: ",
    paste(missing_objects, collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

cat("\nTraining objects loaded successfully.\n")

cat("\nBest glmnet tuning parameters:\n")
print(model_glmnet$bestTune)

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 3: Extract model-specific features

This chunk retrieves the predictors required by each model and prepares training-derived medians for external-data imputation.

```{r b6-module-3-extract-model-specific-features}
get_model_features <- function(model, fallback_ml_df = ml_df) {
  
  if (!is.null(model$trainingData)) {
    features <- setdiff(colnames(model$trainingData), ".outcome")
  } else {
    features <- setdiff(colnames(fallback_ml_df), "group")
  }
  
  return(features)
}

features_glmnet <- get_model_features(model_glmnet)
features_rf <- get_model_features(model_rf)
features_svm <- get_model_features(model_svm)

all_training_features <- unique(c(
  features_glmnet,
  features_rf,
  features_svm
))

cat("\nNumber of model features:\n")
cat("Elastic-net:", length(features_glmnet), "\n")
cat("Random Forest:", length(features_rf), "\n")
cat("Radial SVM:", length(features_svm), "\n")
cat("All unique features:", length(all_training_features), "\n")

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 4: Prepare training medians for missing-value imputation

This chunk retrieves the predictors required by each model and prepares training-derived medians for external-data imputation.

```{r b6-module-4-prepare-training-medians-for-miss}
training_medians <- sapply(
  ml_df[, all_training_features, drop = FALSE],
  function(x) median(as.numeric(x), na.rm = TRUE)
)

training_medians[is.na(training_medians)] <- 0.5

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 5: Load TCGA full myLoad object

This chunk loads the TCGA test object and extracts its beta matrix and phenotype table.

```{r b6-module-5-load-tcga-full-myload-object}
env <- new.env()
loaded_objects <- load(tcga_full_file, envir = env)

if (!"myLoad" %in% loaded_objects) {
  stop(paste0(
    "Object myLoad was not found in: ",
    tcga_full_file,
    ". Objects found: ",
    paste(loaded_objects, collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

myLoad_tcga <- env$myLoad

if (!"beta" %in% names(myLoad_tcga)) {
  stop("myLoad$beta was not found in TCGA full cohort file.")
}

if (!"pd" %in% names(myLoad_tcga)) {
  stop("myLoad$pd was not found in TCGA full cohort file.")
}

beta_tcga <- as.matrix(myLoad_tcga$beta)
storage.mode(beta_tcga) <- "numeric"

pd_tcga <- as.data.frame(myLoad_tcga$pd)

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 6: Align TCGA phenotype table with beta matrix

This chunk constructs the phenotype table and assigns each sample to the relevant analysis group.

```{r b6-module-6-align-tcga-phenotype-table-with-b}
if ("ID" %in% colnames(pd_tcga) && setequal(as.character(pd_tcga$ID), colnames(beta_tcga))) {
  rownames(pd_tcga) <- as.character(pd_tcga$ID)
}

if (setequal(rownames(pd_tcga), colnames(beta_tcga))) {
  pd_tcga <- pd_tcga[colnames(beta_tcga), , drop = FALSE]
}

if (!identical(rownames(pd_tcga), colnames(beta_tcga))) {
  stop("Sample alignment failed between TCGA beta and pd.")
}

if (!"group" %in% colnames(pd_tcga)) {
  stop("Column group was not found in TCGA pd.")
}

if (!all(as.character(pd_tcga$group) %in% c("Tumor", "Normal"))) {
  stop("Unexpected group labels found in TCGA pd.")
}

pd_tcga$group <- factor(
  as.character(pd_tcga$group),
  levels = c("Tumor", "Normal")
)

cat("\nTCGA full cohort sample distribution:\n")
print(table(pd_tcga$group, useNA = "ifany"))

if ("project" %in% colnames(pd_tcga)) {
  print(table(pd_tcga$project, pd_tcga$group))
}

cat("\nTCGA beta dimension:\n")
print(dim(beta_tcga))

cat("\nTCGA pd dimension:\n")
print(dim(pd_tcga))

## Map model-required features back to original DMR IDs
testing_feature_map <- feature_name_map[
  match(all_training_features, feature_name_map$Feature),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (any(is.na(testing_feature_map$DMR_id))) {
  stop("Some model-required features could not be mapped back to DMR IDs.")
}

testing_dmr_ids <- testing_feature_map$DMR_id

testing_dmr_idx <- match(
  testing_dmr_ids,
  dmr.tbl$DMR_id
)

if (any(is.na(testing_dmr_idx))) {
  stop("Some model-required DMR IDs were not found in dmr.tbl.")
}

dmr.tbl.testing <- dmr.tbl[
  testing_dmr_idx,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

dmr.cpg.list.testing <- dmr.cpg.list[
  testing_dmr_idx
]
```

Interpretation: the group-frequency table should contain the expected sample classes without unexpected or missing labels.

### Module 7: Build TCGA DMR-level beta matrix

This chunk aggregates CpG beta values into DMR-level features, handles missing values, and records the feature-name mapping.

```{r b6-module-7-build-tcga-dmr-level-beta-matrix}
dmr_beta_mat <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = ncol(beta_tcga),
  ncol = nrow(dmr.tbl.testing)
)

rownames(dmr_beta_mat) <- colnames(beta_tcga)
colnames(dmr_beta_mat) <- dmr.tbl.testing$DMR_id

for (i in seq_len(nrow(dmr.tbl.testing))) {
  
  cpgs_present <- intersect(
    dmr.cpg.list.testing[[i]],
    rownames(beta_tcga)
  )
  
  if (length(cpgs_present) > 0) {
    dmr_beta_mat[, i] <- colMeans(
      beta_tcga[cpgs_present, , drop = FALSE],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }
}

dmr_beta_mat[is.nan(dmr_beta_mat)] <- NA_real_

```

Interpretation: the coverage summaries indicate how many candidate DMRs can be represented by available array probes, while the resulting matrix supplies the model predictors.

### Module 8: Check CpG coverage in TCGA full cohort

This chunk performs the operations described in **Module 8: Check CpG coverage in TCGA full cohort**.

```{r b6-module-8-check-cpg-coverage-in-tcga-full-c}
cpg_coverage <- data.frame(
  DMR_id = dmr.tbl.testing$DMR_id,
  nCpG_present_TCGA_full = sapply(
    dmr.cpg.list.testing,
    function(x) length(intersect(x, rownames(beta_tcga)))
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

fwrite(
  cpg_coverage,
  file = file.path(
    outdir,
    "TCGA_full_DMR_CpG_coverage.csv"
  )
)

cat("\nCpG coverage summary in TCGA full cohort:\n")
print(summary(cpg_coverage$nCpG_present_TCGA_full))

cat("\nNumber of DMRs with zero CpG coverage in TCGA:\n")
print(sum(cpg_coverage$nCpG_present_TCGA_full == 0))

zero_coverage <- cpg_coverage$nCpG_present_TCGA_full == 0

if (any(zero_coverage)) {
  
  zero_dmr <- cpg_coverage$DMR_id[zero_coverage]
  
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Some model-required DMRs have zero CpG coverage in TCGA: ",
      paste(zero_dmr, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

```

Interpretation: the coverage summaries indicate how many candidate DMRs can be represented by available array probes, while the resulting matrix supplies the model predictors.

### Module 9: Map DMR IDs to training feature names

This chunk maps DMR intervals to annotated CpG probes and summarizes probe availability in the dataset.

```{r b6-module-9-map-dmr-ids-to-training-feature-n}
feature_names <- feature_name_map$Feature[
  match(colnames(dmr_beta_mat), feature_name_map$DMR_id)
]

if (any(is.na(feature_names))) {
  missing_dmr_ids <- colnames(dmr_beta_mat)[is.na(feature_names)]
  stop(paste0(
    "Some TCGA DMRs could not be mapped to training feature names: ",
    paste(head(missing_dmr_ids, 20), collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

colnames(dmr_beta_mat) <- feature_names

missing_features <- setdiff(all_training_features, colnames(dmr_beta_mat))

if (length(missing_features) > 0) {
  stop(paste0(
    "These training features are missing in TCGA matrix: ",
    paste(missing_features, collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

dmr_beta_mat <- dmr_beta_mat[, all_training_features, drop = FALSE]

```

Interpretation: review the printed checks and generated objects before proceeding to the next analysis stage.

### Module 10: Impute missing values using training medians

This chunk retrieves the predictors required by each model and prepares training-derived medians for external-data imputation.

```{r b6-module-10-impute-missing-values-using-trai}
for (fn in all_training_features) {
  
  if (any(is.na(dmr_beta_mat[, fn]))) {
    dmr_beta_mat[is.na(dmr_beta_mat[, fn]), fn] <- training_medians[fn]
  }
}

if (any(is.na(dmr_beta_mat))) {
  stop("There are still missing values after imputation.")
}

```

Interpretation: successful completion means no missing predictor values remain before external prediction.

This chunk assembles the final external-test data frame and saves the corresponding DMR-level feature matrix.


### Module 12: Helper function to evaluate one model

This chunk defines helper functions used to standardize inputs and support the downstream workflow.

```{r b6-module-12-helper-function-to-evaluate-one-}
evaluate_one_model <- function(model, model_name, test_df, model_features) {
  
  x_test <- test_df[, model_features, drop = FALSE]
  
  prob <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = x_test,
    type = "prob"
  )
  
  pred_class <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = x_test,
    type = "raw"
  )
  
  obs <- factor(
    as.character(test_df$group),
    levels = c("Tumor", "Normal")
  )
  
  pred_class <- factor(
    as.character(pred_class),
    levels = c("Tumor", "Normal")
  )
  
  roc_obj <- roc(
    response = obs,
    predictor = prob$Tumor,
    levels = c("Normal", "Tumor"),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )
  
  auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  
  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    data = pred_class,
    reference = obs,
    positive = "Tumor"
  )
  
  performance <- data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    AUC = auc_value,
    Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
    Specificity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
    Balanced_Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    Sample = rownames(test_df),
    Observed = obs,
    Predicted = pred_class,
    Prob_Tumor = prob$Tumor,
    Prob_Normal = prob$Normal,
    Model = model_name,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(list(
    performance = performance,
    predictions = pred_df,
    roc = roc_obj,
    confusion_matrix = cm
  ))
}

```

Interpretation: these functions do not produce a biological result directly; they standardize inputs and enforce consistent processing.

### 🍁🍁 Module 13: Test three models in TCGA full cohort

This chunk applies each trained classifier to the external cohort using its required feature set.

```{r b6-module-13-test-three-models-in-tcga-full-c}
res_glmnet_full <- evaluate_one_model(
  model = model_glmnet,
  model_name = "Elastic-net",
  test_df = test_df_full,
  model_features = features_glmnet
)

res_rf_full <- evaluate_one_model(
  model = model_rf,
  model_name = "Random Forest",
  test_df = test_df_full,
  model_features = features_rf
)

res_svm_full <- evaluate_one_model(
  model = model_svm,
  model_name = "Radial SVM",
  test_df = test_df_full,
  model_features = features_svm
)

```

Interpretation: the returned objects contain the sample-level predictions and the metrics required for model comparison.

### Module 14: Combine and save performance results

This chunk combines the performance and prediction results from the three classifiers and saves the corresponding evaluation outputs.

```{r b6-module-14-combine-and-save-performance-res}
performance_full <- rbind(
  res_glmnet_full$performance,
  res_rf_full$performance,
  res_svm_full$performance
)

predictions_full <- rbind(
  res_glmnet_full$predictions,
  res_rf_full$predictions,
  res_svm_full$predictions

fwrite(
  performance_full,
  file = file.path(outdir,"TCGA_full_model_performance.csv"
))

fwrite(
  predictions_full,
  file = file.path(outdir,"TCGA_full_model_predictions.csv"
))

  res_glmnet_full$confusion_matrix,

))

capture.output(
  res_rf_full$confusion_matrix,

capture.output(

```

Interpretation: higher ROC, sensitivity, and specificity indicate stronger discrimination, but external-cohort results remain the primary validation evidence.

### Module 15: Plot ROC curves for three models

This chunk prepares ROC coordinates and generates the ROC visualization for the three models.

```{r b6-module-15-plot-roc-curves-for-three-models}
roc_to_df <- function(roc_obj, model_name, auc_value) {
  
  df <- data.frame(
    FPR = 1 - roc_obj$specificities,
    TPR = roc_obj$sensitivities,
    Model = paste0(model_name, " (AUC = ", sprintf("%.4f", auc_value), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  df <- df[order(df$FPR, df$TPR), ]
  
  return(df)
}

roc_df_full <- rbind(
  roc_to_df(
    res_glmnet_full$roc,
    "Elastic-net",
    res_glmnet_full$performance$AUC
  ),
  roc_to_df(
    res_rf_full$roc,
    "Random Forest",
    res_rf_full$performance$AUC
  ),
  roc_to_df(
    res_svm_full$roc,
    "Radial SVM",
    res_svm_full$performance$AUC
  )
)
```

Interpretation: curves closer to the upper-left corner and larger AUC values indicate better separation of Tumor and Normal samples.

### Module 16: Plot model performance heatmap

This chunk reshapes the performance table and displays the main evaluation metrics as a heatmap.

```{r b6-module-16-plot-model-performance-heatmap}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

performance_heat <- performance_full[, c(
  "Model",
  "AUC",
  "Accuracy",
  "Sensitivity",
  "Specificity",
  "Balanced_Accuracy"
)]

performance_heat <- as.data.table(performance_heat)

performance_heat <- data.table::melt(
  performance_heat,
  id.vars = "Model",
  variable.name = "Metric",
  value.name = "Value"
)

performance_heat$Metric <- factor(
  performance_heat$Metric,
  levels = c("AUC", "Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Balanced_Accuracy"),
  labels = c("AUC", "Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Balanced accuracy")
)

performance_heat$Model <- factor(
  performance_heat$Model,
  levels = c("Elastic-net", "Random Forest", "Radial SVM")
)
```

Interpretation: the annotations allow small differences among otherwise high-performing models to be compared directly.

# 🍁🍁External validation in the TCGA balanced cohort

The same three models are evaluated in the balanced TCGA cohort to assess performance under a less imbalanced class distribution.

```{r b7-module-3-extract-model-specific-features}

get_model_features <- function(model, fallback_ml_df = ml_df) {
  
  if (!is.null(model$trainingData)) {
    features <- setdiff(colnames(model$trainingData), ".outcome")
  } else {
    features <- setdiff(colnames(fallback_ml_df), "group")
  }
  
  return(features)
}

features_glmnet <- get_model_features(model_glmnet)
features_rf <- get_model_features(model_rf)
features_svm <- get_model_features(model_svm)

all_training_features <- unique(c(
  features_glmnet,

  features_svm
))
```

### Module 6: Align TCGA phenotype table with beta matrix

This chunk constructs the phenotype table and assigns each sample to the relevant analysis group.

```{r b7-module-6-align-tcga-phenotype-table-with-b}

if ("ID" %in% colnames(pd_tcga) && setequal(as.character(pd_tcga$ID), colnames(beta_tcga))) {

}

}

cat("\nTCGA pd dimension:\n")

## Map model-required features back to original DMR IDs
testing_feature_map <- feature_name_map[
  match(all_training_features, feature_name_map$Feature),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (any(is.na(testing_feature_map$DMR_id))) {

}

testing_dmr_ids <- testing_feature_map$DMR_id

testing_dmr_idx <- match(
  testing_dmr_ids,
  dmr.tbl$DMR_id
)

if (any(is.na(testing_dmr_idx))) {
  stop("Some model-required DMR IDs were not found in dmr.tbl.")
}

dmr.tbl.testing <- dmr.tbl[
  testing_dmr_idx,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

dmr.cpg.list.testing <- dmr.cpg.list[
  testing_dmr_idx
]
```

Interpretation: the group-frequency table should contain the expected sample classes without unexpected or missing labels.

### Module 7: Build TCGA DMR-level beta matrix

This chunk aggregates CpG beta values into DMR-level features, handles missing values, and records the feature-name mapping.

```{r b7-module-7-build-tcga-dmr-level-beta-matrix}
dmr_beta_mat <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = ncol(beta_tcga),
  ncol = nrow(dmr.tbl.testing)
)

rownames(dmr_beta_mat) <- colnames(beta_tcga)
colnames(dmr_beta_mat) <- dmr.tbl.testing$DMR_id

for (i in seq_len(nrow(dmr.tbl.testing))) {
  
  cpgs_present <- intersect(
    dmr.cpg.list.testing[[i]],
    rownames(beta_tcga)
  )
  
  if (length(cpgs_present) > 0) {
    dmr_beta_mat[, i] <- colMeans(
      beta_tcga[cpgs_present, , drop = FALSE],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }
}

dmr_beta_mat[is.nan(dmr_beta_mat)] <- NA_real_

```

Interpretation: the coverage summaries indicate how many candidate DMRs can be represented by available array probes, while the resulting matrix supplies the model predictors.

### Module 10: Impute missing values using training medians

This chunk retrieves the predictors required by each model and prepares training-derived medians for external-data imputation.

```{r b7-module-10-impute-missing-values-using-trai}

for (fn in all_training_features) {
```

### Module 12: Helper function to evaluate one model

This chunk defines helper functions used to standardize inputs and support the downstream workflow.

```{r b7-module-12-helper-function-to-evaluate-one-}
evaluate_one_model <- function(model, model_name, test_df, model_features) {
  
  x_test <- test_df[, model_features, drop = FALSE]
  
  prob <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = x_test,
    type = "prob"
  )
  
  pred_class <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = x_test,
    type = "raw"
  )
  
  obs <- factor(
    as.character(test_df$group),
    levels = c("Tumor", "Normal")
  )
  
  pred_class <- factor(
    as.character(pred_class),
    levels = c("Tumor", "Normal")
  )
  
  roc_obj <- roc(
    response = obs,
    predictor = prob$Tumor,
    levels = c("Normal", "Tumor"),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )
  
  auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  
  cm <- confusionMatrix(
    data = pred_class,
    reference = obs,
    positive = "Tumor"
  )
  
  performance <- data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    AUC = auc_value,
    Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    Sensitivity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
    Specificity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
    Balanced_Accuracy = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    Sample = rownames(test_df),
    Observed = obs,
    Predicted = pred_class,
    Prob_Tumor = prob$Tumor,
    Prob_Normal = prob$Normal,
    Model = model_name,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(list(
    performance = performance,
    predictions = pred_df,
    roc = roc_obj,
    confusion_matrix = cm
  ))
}

```

Interpretation: these functions do not produce a biological result directly; they standardize inputs and enforce consistent processing.

```{r b7-module-15-plot-roc-curves-for-three-models-5}

############################################################
## Zoomed ROC plot for TCGA balanced cohort
############################################################

## Rebuild ROC dataframe using 4 decimal places for AUC
roc_to_df <- function(roc_obj, model_name, auc_value) {
  
  df <- data.frame(
    FPR = 1 - roc_obj$specificities,
    TPR = roc_obj$sensitivities,
    Model = paste0(model_name, " (AUC = ", sprintf("%.4f", auc_value), ")"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  df <- df[order(df$FPR, df$TPR), ]
  
  return(df)
}

roc_df_balanced <- rbind(
  roc_to_df(
    res_glmnet_balanced$roc,
    "Elastic-net",
    res_glmnet_balanced$performance$AUC
  ),
  roc_to_df(
    res_rf_balanced$roc,
    "Random Forest",
    res_rf_balanced$performance$AUC
  ),
  roc_to_df(
    res_svm_balanced$roc,
    "Radial SVM",
    res_svm_balanced$performance$AUC
  )
)
```

### Module 16: Plot model performance barplot

This chunk performs the operations described in **Module 16: Plot model performance barplot**.

```{r b7-module-16-plot-model-performance-barplot}
############################################################
## Module 16. Plot model performance barplot
## Fixed version using data.table::melt
############################################################
if(F){performance_long <- performance_balanced[, c(
  "Model",
  "AUC",
  "Accuracy",
  "Sensitivity",
  "Specificity",
  "Balanced_Accuracy"
)]

## Convert data.frame to data.table before melt
performance_long <- as.data.table(performance_long)

performance_long <- data.table::melt(
  performance_long,
  id.vars = "Model",
  variable.name = "Metric",
  value.name = "Value"
)

performance_long$Metric <- factor(
  performance_long$Metric,
  levels = c("AUC", "Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Balanced_Accuracy"),
  labels = c("AUC", "Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Balanced accuracy")
)

p_perf_balanced <- ggplot(
  performance_long,
  aes(x = Model, y = Value, fill = Metric)
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", Value)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.3,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.95, 1.00), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Model performance in TCGA balanced cohort",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Performance",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )

p_perf_balanced

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(outdir,"TCGA_balanced_model_performance_barplot.png"),
  plot = p_perf_balanced,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)}
```
